How the quality score works

Every document gets a score from 0 to 100, shown as a ring under the top bar. Click the ring to open the Quality tab: five bars, what the document already has, and the next steps with the points each one adds. Hover over any item for a tip; click it to come to its section on this page.

The score measures structure, metadata, links and age. It does not check that the content is correct.

Tiers

Tier Score Look
Exemplary 75 and up gold ring, a gold line under the top bar and a note
Complete 60 to 74 green ring
Basic 40 to 59 grey ring
Stub under 40 grey ring
Retired Status Obsolete, Deprecated, Withdrawn, Rejected no score

Records (documents with a WorkType: changes, incidents, tasks, meetings) are short by nature. They are judged by the sections of their WorkType skeleton instead of the shape of a DocType, need 60 words instead of 150 to 800, and get points for a final status instead of a recent date. A record is compared with records of the same WorkType.

Findable (15 points)

Can a reader find the document and know what it is? Points for the frontmatter keys, known values and a Summary.

Core keys

What it checks. The frontmatter has the core keys: Author, Date, DocType, Category, Status, Tag, Topic, Scope and Product.

How to meet it. Add each missing key to the frontmatter, between the two --- lines at the top of the file. One point per key.

markdown 
---
Author: Ana Pérez
Date: 2026-10-24
DocType: How-to guide
Category: Procedure
Status: Released
Tag: certificate, renewal
Topic: Security
Scope: SAP Administration
Product: ADS
---

Known values

What it checks. Status, Priority and DocType use values the theme knows, so lists, colours and filters work.

How to meet it. Use one of these values. Status: New, Open, Draft, Planned, Completed, Released, Finished, Successful, Deprecated, Obsolete, Withdrawn, Rejected. Priority: Critical, Very high, High, Medium, Normal, Low. DocType: Tutorial, How-to guide, Reference, Explanation. The list is in the quality block of theme.json.

markdown 
Status: Released
Priority: Normal
DocType: How-to guide

Summary

What it checks. A one-sentence Summary says what the document is for. It shows under the title, in search results and in link previews.

How to meet it. Add a Summary key with one sentence. Put it in double quotes when it contains a colon.

markdown 
Summary: "Renew the Adobe ReaderRights credential before it expires and register it in ADS."

Structured (25 points)

Is it organised like its kind? Points for sections, a first section that gives context, the shape of its type and the sections of its skeleton.

Two or more sections

What it checks. The body is split into ## sections, so readers can skim it and the table of contents works.

How to meet it. Start each part with a level-2 heading. One section gives 3 of the 5 points.

markdown 
## Description

What this is about.

## Steps

1. First step.

Opens with context

What it checks. The first section gives context: Description, Introduction, Overview, Summary, Objective, Context or Problem.

How to meet it. Make the first ## section one of those names, and say in a few lines what the document is for and when to use it.

markdown 
## Introduction

The ReaderRights credential expires every year. This guide renews it.

Fits its DocType

What it checks. The body has the shape of its DocType.

How to meet it. How-to guide: three or more numbered steps, or a command in a code block. Tutorial: both. Reference: a table, or a list of five or more items. Explanation: three or more sections. Without a DocType, set one first.

markdown 
1. Open transaction SU01.
2. Enter the user name.
3. Click Change.

```bash
sapcontrol -nr 00 -function GetProcessList
```

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| login/min_password_lng | 8 |

Skeleton sections

What it checks. The document has the sections of its skeleton, the template for its Category or WorkType.

How to meet it. Add each missing section as a ## heading, with its content. Similar names count: Overview also matches Description, Introduction or Information; Impact matches Scope, Risk or Justification; Rollback matches Fallback or Backout; Verification matches Validation or Check; Resolution matches Solution or Fix. A References section in a skeleton is scored once, under Connected. The skeletons are listed at the end of this page.

markdown 
## Timeline

- 09:10 Alert received.
- 09:25 Service restarted.

Three or more sections

What it checks. Documents without a skeleton for their Category get full points with three or more sections.

How to meet it. Split the content into at least three ## sections, or set a Category that has a skeleton.

markdown 
## Description

## Steps

## References

No empty sections

What it checks. Every heading has content under it.

How to meet it. Write something under the empty heading, or remove the heading. Each empty section costs 3 points, at most 6.

markdown 
## Rollback

Restore the previous kernel from /usr/sap/SID/SYS/exe/old.

No skeleton text left

What it checks. The example text of the skeleton, such as "Step one" or "List prerequisites here.", has been replaced.

How to meet it. Replace every line of example text from the skeleton with your own content.

Complete (25 points)

Is there enough of it? Points for words, up to the target of its type.

Long enough for its type

What it checks. The body reaches the word target of its type: how-to guide 150, reference 200, explanation 500, tutorial 800, records 60. Code blocks do not count.

How to meet it. Explain the why, the prerequisites and the result, not only the commands. A document under 50 words (records: 20) gets at most 3 points. Words beyond the target add nothing.

Connected (15 points)

Is it part of the knowledge base? Points for links to and from other documents, sources, references and images.

Other documents link to it

What it checks. At least one other document links to this one, so readers can reach it by following links.

How to meet it. In a related document, add a link to this file. The page then lists it under "Linked from".

markdown 
See also [Renew the ReaderRights credential](SAP-BC-ADS-READERRIGHTS.md).

Links to a related document

What it checks. The document links to another document of the knowledge base.

How to meet it. Link to the file name with the .md extension. KB4IT turns it into a link to the page. A link to a section adds # and the section id.

markdown 
Before you start, [stop the batch jobs](SAP-BC-TSK-SUSPEND-JOBS.md#steps).

Cites a source

What it checks. The document cites an external source: an SAP note, vendor documentation, a ticket.

How to meet it. Add a web link. SAP notes named in the text ("note 736902") are also shown in the Details tab.

markdown 
See [SAP Note 736902](https://me.sap.com/notes/736902) and the [ADS documentation](https://help.sap.com/docs/).

References section

What it checks. A section named References, Documentation or Related collects the links.

How to meet it. Add a ## References section at the end, with one link per line.

markdown 
## References

- [SAP Note 736902](https://me.sap.com/notes/736902)
- [Restore the database](RESTORE-DB.md)

Image or diagram

What it checks. The document has an image or a diagram.

How to meet it. Copy the image to source/resources/images/ and link it with a descriptive alt text, which becomes the caption. A Mermaid code block also counts.

markdown 
![User list in transaction SU01](resources/images/su01-users.png)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Alert] --> B[Restart]
```

Working links

What it checks. Every link to another document points to a document that exists.

How to meet it. Check the file name and its .md extension, or create the missing document. Each broken link costs 3 points. kb4it verify lists them all.

markdown 
[Restore the database](RESTORE-DB.md)

Images present

What it checks. Every image the document shows exists in the source folder.

How to meet it. Copy the file to the path in the link, under source/, or correct the path. Each missing image costs 3 points; the page shows a grey box instead.

markdown 
![Transport log](resources/images/stms-log.png)

Current (20 points)

Can a reader trust it today? Points for a final status and a recent Date.

Final status

What it checks. The Status is final: Released, Completed, Finished or Successful.

How to meet it. When the document is ready, set a final status. A draft or an open item gets fewer points (records: 10 of 20).

markdown 
Status: Released

Recently reviewed

What it checks. The Date is recent. The points halve every 3 years for how-to guides and tutorials, 4 for references and 8 for explanations. Records do not lose points with age.

How to meet it. Review the content: check commands, versions and screenshots. Then set the Date to the day of the review.

markdown 
Date: 2026-10-24

Dated

What it checks. The document has a Date in a format KB4IT reads.

How to meet it. Add a Date key as YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

markdown 
Date: 2026-10-24

Skeletons

A skeleton is the template the Add page starts a document from. The quality score checks that a document has the ## sections of its skeleton: records use the skeleton of their WorkType, other documents the skeleton of their first Category.

# Title of the change

## Overview

Describe the change: what, where, when and why.

## Impact

Describe the systems and users affected, and the downtime.

## Rollback

Describe how to undo the change if it fails.

# Title of the incident

## Summary

Summarise what failed, for whom and for how long.

## Timeline

- HH:MM Describe the first event, such as the alert.
- HH:MM Describe the next event, up to the recovery.

Explain why it failed.

## Attendees

- List each attendee with their role.

## Agenda

- Describe the first agenda item.
- Describe the next agenda item.

## Notes

Record the discussion and the decisions taken.

## Action Items

# Title of the procedure

## Introduction

Say what this procedure achieves and when to use it.

## Prerequisites

- Access, role or authorisation needed.
- Systems, tools or files needed before you start.

## Steps

1. Describe the first step.
2. Describe the second step.
3. Describe the third step.

```bash
replace-with-the-command --and-its-options
```

## Verification

Explain how to check that the procedure worked.

## References

- [SAP Note 0000000](https://me.sap.com/notes/0000000)
